edits.prompt:
Use case: text-localization / scientific-educational. EDIT the provided diagram as the base, preserving its polished white background, navy sans-serif typography, soft blue/orange/teal fills, thin borders, shared student backbone and two-row composition. This is an actual blog diagram, not a mockup. Keep crisp large labels at blog size. Landscape 16:9.
Main goal: unmistakably show OFF-POLICY expert demonstrations being transformed into student-aligned ON-POLICY training data, then used in ordinary student SFT. Few words, correct arrows.
Title exactly: "Off-policy expert data → On-policy training data".
Top row: heading "Sampling mode"; left blue box contains "Prompt x" and "Expert trace τ", with a prominent small label above it "OFF-POLICY". Arrow goes LEFT to RIGHT into shared central student backbone; orange badge above arrow "LoRA on". Center large blue box label "Student backbone pθ"; orange inset label "LoRA sampler qφ". Top-right teal output box label "On-policy data y"; smaller second line "verified · student-aligned". These are samples from a learned approximation to the expert-constrained current student policy, not guaranteed samples from the unconstrained student. A concise footer says exactly "Match the student; preserve the expert information."
Bottom row: heading "Student mode"; left blue box "Prompt x"; arrow LEFT to RIGHT into same backbone with gray "LoRA off" badge. Right teal box "Score / SFT". Add a clear separate down arrow FROM the top-right data box TO the bottom-right Score / SFT box labeled "training data", so the reader sees generated y is what the student learns from. This arrow does not run into the expert input. Retain direct central-backbone-to-Score/SFT arrow. Use pθ and qφ typographic subscripts properly.
Do not add metrics, models, invented losses, unrelated decoration or extra steps. Do not use generic "generate data". Use exactly the labels specified. Maintain reference style while reducing wasted whitespace enough for good mobile readability.

Use case: text-localization / scientific-educational. EDIT this provided circular online-training diagram, preserving its elegant white background, navy sans-serif typography, orange sampler box, teal data box, blue SFT box, and clockwise curved arrows. Landscape 16:9, crisp large text, balanced spacing. Main goal is to make off-policy expert data → on-policy student-aligned training data explicit without verbosity.
Title exactly "Online: turn expert data into on-policy data".
Keep three stages in a CLOCKWISE loop: top ORANGE "Fit LoRA sampler"; right TEAL "On-policy data" with smaller line "student-aligned · verified"; lower-left BLUE "SFT student". Clear arrows: Fit LoRA sampler → On-policy data → SFT student → Fit LoRA sampler. The return arrow from SFT student to sampler is labeled "updated student". Label the arrow from sampler to data "transform".
Add one compact input box just outside the loop upper left reading "Off-policy" then "expert data". Feed it with one clearly directed arrow into the Fit LoRA sampler box. This is a fixed expert-data input, distinct from the student feedback. Do NOT imply that expert data are newly regenerated each round. The orange sampler and blue student share one backbone; training phases alternate.
Center of loop small repeat symbol with "repeat". Footer exactly "Refresh the sampler as the student changes."
Only these concise labels. No generic "generate data", no extra boxes or metrics, no phantom arrows. Output data approximate the expert-constrained student distribution; the concise descriptor student-aligned expresses this without a long equation. Keep diagram technical and self-contained, use the provided image as the edit target rather than inventing a different art style.

Edit the supplied LoRA infographic into a MOBILE portrait layout, approximately 4:5 aspect ratio. Preserve white background, navy large sans-serif typography and original blue/orange/teal box styling. Reflow, do not crop. Exact heading on two lines "Off-policy expert data" then "→ On-policy training data". Four vertically stacked stages with LARGE, readable labels and bold clear DOWNWARD arrows:
1. Blue input box: "Off-policy expert data"; small line "Prompt x + expert trace τ".
2. Large pale-blue box "Student backbone pθ" with orange inset "LoRA sampler qφ", with orange badge "LoRA on" above the box. This is the same shared backbone as in the provided figure.
3. Teal box "On-policy data y"; small line "verified · student-aligned".
4. Blue/teal SFT operation box "Score / SFT", gray badge "LoRA off"; small line "Prompt x + data y".
Arrow 3→4 labeled "training data". The last box is an operation on the SAME backbone with its adapter disabled, not another model; a small line beneath it says "Same backbone, adapter disabled". Keep one and only one explicit backbone box. Expert trace τ is absent from the bottom SFT conditioning. The remaining student's conditional scoring uses prompt x and generated candidate y. Concise footer exactly "Preserve expert information; match the student."
The mobile figure shows the data-conversion flow and two adapter modes without tiny labels or dense explanations. All labels must be large enough to read when rendered at 350 pixels wide: primary text at least 44px per 1024px canvas width, secondary at least 34px, margins under 45px. No other details or symbols. Output PNG portrait. The provided picture is the editing target.

Edit the supplied online-loop infographic into a MOBILE portrait layout, about 4:5 aspect ratio, white background and the same navy typography, orange sampler, teal on-policy data, blue SFT and gray expert data as the provided picture. Reflow, do not crop.
Large exact heading on two lines "Online: expert data" then "→ on-policy data".
At top below heading one wide input box "Off-policy expert data"; a downward input arrow feeds an orange box "Fit LoRA sampler" near upper center. Below that, two side-by-side LARGE boxes: left blue "SFT student"; right teal "On-policy data", smaller line "verified · student-aligned" (wrap the subtitle into two lines if needed).
A visible CLOCKWISE loop: top orange sampler → lower-right on-policy data (arrow label "transform"); lower-right data → lower-left SFT student (curved arrow below the boxes); lower-left SFT student → upper sampler (curved arrow on left labeled "updated student"). Fixed expert data input stays outside this loop and distinct from student feedback. Center of loop small repeat icon with "repeat" but avoid overcrowding. Footer "Refresh as the student changes."
Primary text at least 44px per 1024px canvas width, secondary at least 34px; heading 55px minimum. Boxes wide enough for short words. Use strong arrowheads and clear separation. The expert input MUST point into the sampler, not into SFT. No loss equations or extra stages. The result needs to be readable at 350 pixels wide. Preserve the provided image's scientific diagram style.

edits.prompt:
EDIT the supplied MCMC versus amortized sampler comparison into a much simpler scientific blog diagram. Reference image 1 is the actual edit target. Reference image 2 is STYLE ONLY: match its white background, navy sans-serif letters, flat soft-blue inputs, soft-orange sampler/search, soft-teal outputs, thin borders and clear navy arrows. No red/green judgement pills, no gradients beyond subtle light box fills, no decorative icons, no density of text. Landscape 16:9. Exact main title "Expert data → More on-policy data". Two balanced side-by-side panels; LARGE text readable at 780px wide.
LEFT panel header "MCMC", short line "Search each example". Show two compact horizontal example rows. Each row has blue expert input labeled "x₁, τ₁" or "x₂, τ₂", orange candidate box labeled "candidate y" with a visible circular search arrow, then a teal output box labeled "verified y". Navy left-to-right arrows. A single label above both candidate loops "Revise · score · accept/reject". These are RESPONSE updates with fixed model weights, not sampler weight training. Bottom one concise line "Repeat the search for each prompt".
RIGHT panel header "Amortized sampler". Top subheading "1. Fit across examples". Blue box "Expert data" plus small label "student scores" feeds orange "Learn sampler qφ". This trains reusable parameters from expert examples, student likelihoods and verification, NOT from MCMC traces. Bottom subheading "2. Reuse the learned sampler". A downward arrow labelled "weights" FROM the top trained-sampler box TO a distinct lower orange box "Sampler qφ". A blue "Expert data" input feeds that lower sampler from the left; the lower sampler feeds a teal "Verified y" output at right. One tiny line under the lower sampler "Construct responses token by token". Final bottom line "Reuse training across prompts".
Single overall footer "Both routes produce verified, student-aligned SFT data."
Do NOT include "faster", "slower", runtime numbers or universal speedup claims. Reduce original text substantially; no three repeated rows, no long explanatory subtitle. Use qφ with subscript phi. Input x and expert τ are off-policy expert examples; outputs approximate the expert-constrained student target. Keep all arrows unambiguous, all panels spacious, and style identical to reference image 2.

edits.prompt:
EDIT the comparison diagram into a MOBILE portrait 4:5 infographic. Actual edit target is reference1; use reference2 ONLY for the exact clean visual style: white background, navy sans-serif type, blue expert inputs, orange search/sampler boxes, teal data outputs, thin borders, strong navy arrows. All labels readable at 350px display width: major labels at least 44px per 1024 canvas width, minor at least 34px.
Title two lines "Expert data →" then "More on-policy data". Two panels stacked TOP and BOTTOM (not side-by-side).
TOP header "MCMC · search each example". Show blue "Off-policy expert data" → orange "Revise candidate y" with a curved self-loop labeled "score · accept/reject" → teal "Verified, student-aligned data". Lay out this flow vertically for legibility. Bottom short line "Repeat the search for each prompt". This loop updates response y with fixed model weights.
BOTTOM header "Amortized sampler · learn to reuse". Blue "Expert data + student scores" → orange "Fit sampler qφ" → orange "Reuse sampler qφ" → teal "Verified, student-aligned data". Lay out vertically, arrow between orange stages labelled "learned weights". Short line within reuse stage "expert traces → responses". Bottom short line "Reuse training across prompts".
No fast/slow slogans, no runtime claims, no three duplicated examples, no long subtitles. Clearly separate fitting shared PARAMETERS from revising a candidate RESPONSE. Do not show MCMC trajectories feeding sampler training. Four concise stages in bottom panel only; arrows clear and padding modest. All labels in the provided image are to be replaced with this simplified wording. Match reference2.

EDIT the supplied offline-process image. Reference 1 is the edit target; reference 2 is STYLE ONLY and sets white background, navy typography, soft blue for student/expert inputs, orange for sampler, teal for output data, fine borders, plain clean arrows. Match the related online and LoRA diagrams. Landscape 16:9. Main exact title "Offline: expert data → more on-policy data".
Keep two broad areas with minimal text. Left area heading "A. Transform the data"; right area heading "B. Train the student". In A, two blue input boxes at far left: top "Off-policy expert data" small "(x, τ)"; bottom "Frozen student pθ". They both feed a single orange stage box "1. Fit sampler qφ". This feeds a teal stage box "2. Transform expert data", with large data label beneath "More on-policy data", smaller "verified · student-aligned". It should be unmistakable that stage 2 consumes the off-policy expert examples too: a simple clear blue arrow from the expert-data input routed above stage 1 directly into stage 2, labelled "expert traces", while the stage1→stage2 arrow is labelled "trained sampler". Keep these routes visually separated and no ambiguous intersections.
One big rightward arrow carries the teal verified dataset into area B's single blue box "3. SFT student". Avoid the original duplicate generated-data box; the teal dataset from A is the training input. Small line beneath A "Student stays fixed"; small line beneath B "Train on the fixed dataset". Overall footer exactly "Fit once. Transform the data. Run SFT."
No return arrow from SFT to sampler (this is offline). No generic standalone "generate data" label. No invented steps, performance claims, complex icons or extra equations. On-policy here means closer to the expert-constrained student distribution, so the wording more on-policy is deliberate. Use the reference's crisp technical styling and large typography.

EDIT reference1's offline process into a MOBILE portrait 4:5 diagram. Reference2 is STYLE ONLY: white background, navy big sans-serif text, soft blue inputs/student, orange sampler, teal data, fine outlines and navy arrows. Large labels readable at 350px width (primary at least 44px / 1024canvas; secondary at least 34px). No dense prose, no generic "generate data".
Exact title on two lines "Offline: expert data" then "→ more on-policy data".
Vertical flow:
Top two inputs side-by-side BLUE boxes: "Off-policy expert data (x, τ)" and "Frozen student pθ". Both arrows converge into orange "1. Fit sampler qφ".
Down arrow labeled "trained sampler" to teal "2. Transform expert data", with "More on-policy data" and smaller "verified · student-aligned" in that same stage box.
An additional thin clearly directed blue arrow from off-policy expert input down the outside-left margin enters stage2, labeled "expert traces"; it bypasses sampler fitting and denotes reuse of expert conditioning during data generation. Avoid crossing the central arrows.
Down arrow from teal data stage to blue "3. SFT student", smaller line "fixed dataset".
A small label beside stages1–2 says "student fixed" if space allows; no need to repeat pθ many times.
Footer "Fit once. Transform data. Run SFT."
No return arrows; no feedback to sampler after student SFT. No extra duplicate dataset box, no decorative icons or exact-policy guarantees. The wording more on-policy is intentional. Match reference2 closely.
